title: Ottoman, Arabic and Persian structures
summary: Recognize the Arabic and Persian building blocks that Ottoman Turkish left in today's language: the izafet (*aşk-ı memnu*, *hüsnüniyet*), the Arabic article (*bilhassa*, *maalesef*), Arabic plurals, the adjective suffix -î (*millî*, *resmî*), Persian affixes such as *bî-*, *na-*, *-hane* and *-kâr*, and Arabic root families.
canDo: Read fixed Persian and Arabic phrases in titles, names and formal Turkish
Recognize Arabic plurals and words built on the same Arabic root
Spell adjectives in -î the way TDK does: millî, resmî, but siyasi
Work out words built with bî-, na-, -hane, -dar, -kâr, -zade, -name and -gâh
vocabThemes: the Ottoman court and its offices
